examples.translation: combinare il twirling di Pauli con il dynamical decoupling
examples.suggested: combinare il Pauli twirling con il decoupling dinamico
examples.why: The page renders the term as "decoupling dinamico" everywhere else, but here it slips back to the English "dynamical decoupling".

examples.source: the reason for the spreading of the state in the Bloch sphere picture
examples.translation: la ragione dello spargimento dello stato nella rappresentazione della sfera di Bloch
examples.suggested: la ragione dell'allargamento (dispersione) dello stato sulla sfera di Bloch
examples.why: "Spargimento" suggests literally scattering or spilling something. A physicist would write "allargamento" or "dispersione".

examples.source: the delays in measuring the first/early qubits
examples.translation: i ritardi nella misura dei qubit iniziali/precoci
examples.suggested: i ritardi nella misura dei primi qubit
examples.why: "Precoci" is an unnatural word-for-word rendering of "early" when talking about qubits.

editor_note: Entry 48 is faithful and natural: "Per i dettagli sulle opzioni di mitigazione degli errori, consulta le seguenti guide e il riferimento API" keeps informal "tu", and "Configura la mitigazione degli errori" matches the same link text in entry 42.

Rewritten entry 60 renders the heading "Quantum Machine Learning" as "Apprendimento automatico quantistico". That is correct Italian and does not mislead. The rest of the page keeps the English term, though: entry 48 has "per il machine learning", and the paragraph right under this heading (entry 61) opens with "Nel machine learning" and later says "approcci classici di machine learning". The heading should match the body, for example "Machine learning quantistico".

examples.source: Quantum Machine Learning {#quantum-machine-learning}
examples.translation: Apprendimento automatico quantistico {#quantum-machine-learning}
examples.suggested: Machine learning quantistico {#quantum-machine-learning}
examples.why: The meaning is right, but the term doesn't match the rest of the file. Entries 48 and 61, including the sentence directly under this heading, keep 'machine learning', so the heading and body use two different names for the same field.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries changes the meaning. In entry 20, "shot" and "stringhe di bit recuperate" are faithful. In entry 27, "base degli autostati" matches entry 44, and entry 150's "Estinzione degli errori di lettura mediante twirling (T-REx)" is a defensible heading. The one defect is a grammar slip in entry 27: "Il [`Estimator`]" needs the elided article "L'`Estimator`". The same page already writes "l'`Estimator`" in entries 67 and 82.

examples.source: The IBM Quantum [`Estimator`](...) uses a complex algebraic process
examples.translation: Il [`Estimator`](...) di IBM Quantum utilizza un complesso processo algebrico
examples.suggested: L'[`Estimator`](...) di IBM Quantum utilizza un complesso processo algebrico
examples.why: Italian elides the article before a vowel. 'Il Estimator' is ungrammatical, and it clashes with 'l'`Estimator`' in entries 67 and 82.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The pass rule survives intact ("almeno 16" of 20 correct), as does the two-attempt lockout ("in due tentativi, l'esame verrà temporaneamente bloccato"), and the informal "tu" holds. One wording slip: entry [12] says "il badge IBM Digital Badge", which repeats "badge" and would read better as "un IBM Digital Badge". Also in [12], the final period was moved inside the link text ("[qui.]"). That is cosmetic only.

examples.source: In order to issue you an IBM Digital Badge, your personal information ... will be shared with Credly.
examples.translation: Per il rilascio del badge IBM Digital Badge, le tue informazioni personali ...
examples.suggested: Per rilasciarti un IBM Digital Badge, le tue informazioni personali ...
examples.why: "badge IBM Digital Badge" says "badge" twice. A native editor would drop the extra word and use the more direct verb form.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally in Italian. Entry 64 ("Qui introduciamo il numero di stati che vogliamo calcolare, le penalità e un insieme di parametri iniziali x0") keeps all three items, and entry 65 ("Ora testeremo l'algoritmo usando i simulatori") uses informal register and matches how the rest of the page words simulator use.

The translation is faithful and reads naturally, with a consistent informal "tu" (for example "riceverai una notifica da Credly") and correct terms such as "algoritmi variazionali", "primitive di IBM Quantum" and "elaboratore di dati terzo".
